author: Elendinn
body:
TheyTellMeItRained beat me to it, but here's the run-down I was putting together, with some specific items to look for and some general swashing strategies:

**Equipment** 

Ideally, you want low-defense gear with lots of adornment slots and other valuable stats (attack, mana, ward, etc.) or status immunities that you can bring up to masterforged+ quality and adorn with Crimson or Ashen Pinions (more on that later).

**Head:** Avalon Crown is pretty much best-in-slot; the higher the quality, the better (bonus points for having an element). A low-quality Hallowed Witch's Hat is great for immunity builds (especially for pvp). Aldon's Hat can be useful for stun immunity, and one with an element can be great for Morrigan raids (Aldon's Hat doesn't really benefit from smithing). 

**Chest:** Fey Yeti Coat is basically best-in-slot for its mana and ward (plus water resistance and freeze immunity). Qualities up to famed can be viable, depending on how well you can offset the defense. High-quality Hel's Garb or broken/poor Arisen Hel's Garb can also be serviceable; they don't have hp/mana, but the blind and stun immunities are useful, especially in pvp. 

**Feet:** Random-generated t3 boots are great because they have super low defense and 8 adornment slots when masterforged. Ashen Phoenician Boots are good for ward, but they have really high defense, even at broken quality, so they can be tough to build around. When Naggeneen comes back, Smelly Shoes are really desirable for their poison/blight immunities and adornment slots. Fey Dragon Boots are good for Morrigan raids (dragon resistance plus a few adornment slots). 

**Weapons:** for 1-handers, any of the Badb Cathas from Morrigan/Arisen Morrigan, Arisen Ithra's Blade, Arisen Vulcan's Longsword, Arisen Bow of Typhon, or Nightbreak (for immunity builds). For 2-handers (best used with Arisen Trevelyan Charms): Old Hallowed Blade, Arisen Gandring, or Realmspikes. 

**Off-hands** (for gauntlets/world farming): if you have Arisen Hel's Feathers, the +ward and Volley III make them great for just about everything but raiding; otherwise, you'll probably want an Arisen Shield, primarily for endlesses. Fey Arrows are solid for world farming and Volley III-spamming in the arena. Mighty Griffin Shield can be useful for Morrigan raids if you don't have Fey Dragon Boots, or if you want the dragon resistance plus some additional ward. 

**Accessories:** Arisen Rings for +atk and -def, Ring of Annwn/Briny Pendant for immunities, Arisen Trevelyan Charms for 2-hander builds. 

**Adornments:** use some combination of Crimson and Ashen Pinions in your armor. Crimsons will lower your mana, which is why a Fey Yeti Coat is desirable, but you can also use a few Jewels of the Deep to help offset the mana loss (I find 450ish mana to be pretty viable for most scenarios). Ashens will lower your attack, but will give you +4% crit each, which is very valuable when running endlesses. For crit builds, Ferocious Bull's Eyes are best, followed by Untamed Bull's Eyes and Eyes of the Morrigan. Use them in your 2-hander, or in your off-hand when dual-wielding. Assassin's Jewels and Mammon's Teardrops are great for your main-hand when using a 1-hander.

**Pets:** Chimera/Fey Chimera is best in most scenarios. Orichalcum Golem works really well when running endlesses (for ward recovery), but you'll probably want to let Chimera buff you with Berserk before switching. Ashen Phoenix is desirable for deep endlesses.

**General Advice** 

To get the full swash passive, you'll need to be around 5-10% under your base (naked) defense. Coral gear can be good if you need to offset the defense of other, better pieces of equipment, but, as your build develops and you acquire enough Pinions and some Arisen Rings, you won't need to use Coral very often, if at all.
 
When raiding, you'll generally only use ward for buffing purposes. After that, you'll rely on Osmostrikes II or crits to keep you healed. If you've got a crit build, Realm Strikes is an excellent dps skill (20% base crit + 20% crit from Wyrm's Song + crit from your gear will get you consistent, if not guaranteed, crits). You *can* use a shield for some extra survivability, but dual-wielding is typically preferred for efficiency. 2-handers can work, too, but you'll lose at least one accessory slot to the Trev Charms, which can be detrimental if you need the -def from Arisen Rings, or status immunities from Ring of Annwn/Briny Pendant.
 
In endlesses, you'll want high-ish ward (which can be tough for swashes) + 100% ward absorption from DB1/DB2 so you can redline relatively safely. Use Stun/Sleep Dart on tough enemies that are susceptible. Sortie is great for berserks since it has high penetration and 15% base crit. Use Bleed to recharge your mana (costs 15 mana and has 25% base crit) when necessary.

That's kinda the basic gist of swash, but customizing your build can get a lot more complicated, and strategies and gear/skill loadouts will probably vary a lot depending on what you're up against. Hopefully that helps!

author: [deleted]
body:
The short answer is that there are a LOT of options at your disposal. Any broken item that nullifies status effects like stun, sleep, etc. will be good in one way or another. 

The long answer, just off the top of my head;

Crimson pinions, crimson pinions, crimson pinions

Avalon crown for petrify/curse immunity

Aldon's hat is great too for stun immunity, same with dusk gear

Lunar garb for even more attack. I've heard some people mention Sala's robe as well but personally I prefer Lunar garb.

Don't neglect coral gear. It may be tier 8 but ornate coral gear can grant you a TON of res while keeping your defense as low as possible. 

As for your weapon, the higher the attack the better obviously. Personally I run realmspikes if I want crit or a Badb Cath with Volley III arrows (Arisen Hel's feathers / Fey arrows) The only thing to keep in mind with realmspikes is that with a ton of crimson pinions, your mana will be very low, whereas with a primary + arrows, you can just rely on volley III which costs 0 mana. Most likely both slotted with eyes of morrigan for the stats and crit chance

Accessories, you want good arisen rings. Ornates grant up to an additional +200 attack while dropping your defense even more. Either those or status immunity items like ring of annwn or briny pendant depending on what you're doing

There's a TON more, some of which are event items (like dusk gear) that I didn't mention because of that but that should be a good starting point. As always, Shabbash has some good videos on youtube covering it as well.
